title: On-call Baton: Tiled Wizardlet for Alert Setup and Postmortem Linking
creator: Maya Rios
description:
Problem: On-call responders frequently miss contextual links (runbooks, postmortems, cost impact dashboards) when an alert fires. The current alert-setup flow in Redwood Console surfaces SLO and routing, but postmortem linkage and quick handoff controls are buried in multiple screens. This ticket is to design a compact, tiled ‘On-call Baton’ wizardlet that appears in the final step of alert creation and in the incident panel to streamline handoffs and attach postmortem links

Goals:
- Surface runbook and postmortem attachments at alert creation time and expose lightweight handoff messages for responders.
- Provide a tiled compact UI that fits into the alert composer and the incident side rail without adding > 200ms render cost.
- Allow linking to one or more postmortem drafts, Confluence runbooks, and a short handoff message template.
- Show cost-sensitivity hints (when an alert is likely to trigger large-scale re-runs or retraces) and a small CTA to pin a cost dashboard snapshot.

Scope:
- Prototype Figma frames for the wizardlet in two contexts: Alert Setup modal and Incident Side Rail.
- Microcopy for handoff templates and inline validation.
- Accessibility pass for keyboard + screen reader.
- Lightweight interaction spec for engineering (expand/collapse tiles, quick-select recent postmortems, ephemeral toast confirmation).
updates: 2026-02-15: Kickoff meeting with PM and Eng; aligned on scope and success metrics (reduce time-to-attach-postmortem by 40%). Meeting notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link-oncall-baton-kickoff
2026-02-19: Exploratory sketches completed; two visual directions: 'stacked chips' vs 'tiled concierge'. Team decided to pursue 'tiled concierge' for denser context and affordances.
2026-02-23: First Figma prototype (v0.1) uploaded: https://www.figma.com/file/fakeboard/oncall-baton-v01; includes Alert Setup modal variant and Incident Side Rail variant.

2026-02-24: Design review with Eng (runtime, console rendering team). Feedback: avoid heavy DOM nesting; prefer static tiles with CSS transitions. Action: add interaction spec for collapse state to limit reflows.
2026-02-26: PM review — request to add explicit cost snapshot CTA and default to last 7-day cost window. Added copy and small chart placeholder to tile.
2026-02-27: Accessibility pass notes added: ensure role=region headings, aria-expanded for each tile, keyboard focus order. Added testcases for NVDA and VoiceOver.
2026-03-01: Prototype v0.3 ready for stakeholder review; design PR opened (link to design PR): https://github.com/redwood/inference-console/pull/4567 (design assets attached in Figma).
2026-03-01: Ready for cross-functional review: scheduled review with Reliability and Customer Success on 2026-03-03.
review_feedback: Reliability: like the quick fallback action to silence noisy alerts, requested an explicit prompt to link fallback model or region when relevant.
Customer Success: suggested an 'attach postmortem draft' checkbox to encourage ownership; recommended linking to template for postmortem creation.
Engineering: suggested lazy-loading cost snapshot and deferring chart rendering until tile expansion to reduce initial load.
Security: confirmed no additional data surface is needed; recommended logging when a postmortem link is attached for auditability.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototypes for both contexts (Alert Setup modal and Incident Side Rail) are finalized and tagged with component specs.
Interaction spec enumerated (expand/collapse, quick-select recent artifacts, keyboard flows).
Design handoff PR includes accessible tokens, visual spec, and CSS guidance for minimal reflow.
PM approved copy for handoff templates and cost snapshot CTA.
Engineering PR includes a demo story in Storybook and automated a11y checks passing.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: extra UI in alert flow could increase cognitive load. Mitigation: default tiles collapsed and show a succinct one-line summary; progressive disclosure.
Risk: performance impact when rendering cost snapshots. Mitigation: lazy-load charts and use a lightweight sparkline image when collapsed.
Risk: teams may forget to attach useful artifacts. Mitigation: surface recent postmortems and allow one-click creation of a draft postmortem from the tile.
notes: Design considered two microcopy strategies: minimal (one-line handoff) vs guided (three-step template). Chosen: minimal by default, guided exposed after expansion.
We intentionally avoid exposing full runbook content in the tile to keep surface area small; links open runbooks in a dedicated panel.
Follow-up: create a small usability lab session with 5 on-call engineers during Cycle 11 to validate clickthrough and mean time to attach postmortem.
